output.title: Retrieval quality is a workflow constraint
output.body:
If your AI tool has to look up information to do useful work, retrieval quality is part of the workflow design, not an afterthought. In plain terms: if the system searches documents, emails, FAQs, or past records and pulls back the wrong material, the answer can look tidy and still be wrong. That means rework for you, or a confident mistake. For a small business owner, the real question is not “can AI answer this?” but “can it find the right source every time this task runs?”

A practical rule of thumb is to look at one recurring task and ask how often it forces you to search more than one place for the answer. If that happens regularly, retrieval quality has become a design constraint. Customer questions, invoice checks, and lead follow-up are all examples of the kind of repeat work where this shows up.

The control I would keep is source display: the system should show which document it used before you trust the answer. Bareni’s self-built local knowledge-assistant demo shows grounded answers with sources on synthetic data, but the public route is locked, so treat that as a demo pattern, not a deployed service. The next step is simple: audit the source material for one recurring workflow. Are the documents named clearly, grouped sensibly, and kept current? If not, automating the search will mostly move the manual work earlier.
